name: Entity Ledger
summary: Forty enemies in one script instead of forty script engines — and the four rules that make a ledger safe.
description: A ScriptComponent is a script engine, and one per enemy is the single most expensive thing a wave-based game can do to itself. So an entity here is a row in parallel arrays, its actor carries only a sprite and a collider, and one update walks all of them. Spawning, removal, statuses, separation, contact, area damage and queries come with it; behave() is the one function you write. It also carries the four rules that are easy to get wrong and expensive to rediscover: removal swaps, iterate backwards, a cascade must not recurse, and colliders exist so projectiles can find what they hit.
nextSteps: Put EntityLedger.js on a manager actor and tag it Ledger.
Fill in the KIND_* arrays: one column entry per kind of thing.
Write behave(i, dt, nx, ny, dist, speed) -- that is your game; the rest is machinery.
Implement onEntityKilled(kind, x, y, score) on whatever you set notifyTag to.
Read the four rules at the top before changing anything that can kill.
